title: Inquisitive Conversational Agents: Agentic Systems for Domain-Specific Information Seeking
text: While many conversational systems are designed to respond to the user, some settings require the agent to take control of the conversation and ask the questions. This interaction arises across domains: in medical diagnosis, questions distinguish among possible conditions; in troubleshooting, they isolate the source of a failure; and in legal settings, they examine competing interpretations or establish relevant facts. In each case, the agent has an objective to resolve, but the information needed to reach an answer is distributed across the conversation. This tutorial covers the foundations and recent advances in Inquisitive Conversational Agents (ICAs), bringing together research on agents that strategically control a dialogue through questioning to resolve an underlying state or answer. Unlike information-seeking systems centered on retrieving and ranking external information, ICAs acquire information through successive exchanges with a conversational counterpart. Drawing on information seeking, dialogue systems, sequential decision-making, and agentic AI, we cover methods for selecting and sequencing questions, planning over future interactions, and adapting inquiry strategies based on responses and prior interactions. We also draw on Conversational Control and Planning, Argumentation, and Evidence Attribution to examine how agents direct multi-turn interactions, reason over competing claims, and ground acquired information. Designed for researchers, students, and practitioners, the tutorial provides a unified view of this emerging area and methods for designing agents capable of sustained, goal-directed inquiry.
